_note: The data dictionary the language model is given in scenario 3. It describes the view `txs`, not the real table: the view holds only the columns listed here, for the test period of the IBM AML data (the synthetic dataset HI-Small), so a query can never see the laundering label or any answer-bearing column.
description: One row per payment from one account to another. The data is synthetic.

columns.name: ts
columns.meaning: When the payment was made, to the minute.

columns.name: from_account
columns.meaning: The account the money leaves. An account id such as 80308DE40.

columns.name: to_account
columns.meaning: The account the money arrives in.

columns.name: amount_log
columns.meaning: ln(1 + amount paid). This is a natural logarithm, NOT the amount: an amount of 1000 is stored as about 6.9. Compare amounts with each other through this column, or avoid comparing amounts.

columns.name: is_cross_currency
columns.meaning: True when the payment currency differs from the receiving currency.

columns.name: is_self_transfer
columns.meaning: True when from_account and to_account are the same account.

columns.name: is_same_bank
columns.meaning: True when both accounts are at the same bank.

columns.name: fmt_wire
columns.meaning: 1 when the payment format is a wire transfer, else 0.

columns.name: fmt_ach
columns.meaning: 1 when the payment format is ACH, else 0.

columns.name: fmt_cheque
columns.meaning: 1 when the payment format is a cheque, else 0.

columns.name: fmt_cash
columns.meaning: 1 when the payment format is cash, else 0.

columns.name: fmt_credit_card
columns.meaning: 1 when the payment format is a credit card, else 0.

columns.name: fmt_bitcoin
columns.meaning: 1 when the payment format is bitcoin, else 0.

columns.name: fmt_reinvestment
columns.meaning: 1 when the payment format is a reinvestment, else 0.

notes: There is no table of accounts, customers, companies, invoices, shipments or jurisdictions: only these payments.
A column or table that is not listed here does not exist for you.
The data covers a short period of about two and a half days, so only patterns that complete within that period can be found.
The dialect is DuckDB SQL. Timestamps can be compared with each other and shifted with INTERVAL, for example ts + INTERVAL 2 DAY.

example.pattern: Money that an account receives and passes on to another account within one hour (a different pattern from the one you are asked about).
example.sql: SELECT t1.tx_id FROM txs t1 JOIN txs t2 ON t2.from_account = t1.to_account AND t2.ts > t1.ts AND t2.ts <= t1.ts + INTERVAL 1 HOUR WHERE t1.from_account <> t1.to_account LIMIT 1000
example.note: It only shows the syntax and the expected output: each flagged payment is returned by its tx_id.

data_source.name: Transaction Logs
data_source.note: The AMLTRIX data source this table stands for. A first draft written by people: of the data sources AMLTRIX lists for a technique, the payments table is the one that holds transaction records.
